oneSentence: Tools in this area turn text or voice examples into new spoken audio, from a generic computer voice to a close imitation of a particular person.
plainExplanation:
Audio and speech generation means creating sound with a model rather than recording a person speaking each line. The input might be written text, music instructions, a short voice sample, or all three. The output is an audio file or live spoken sound.

These terms are related but not identical. Text-to-speech, often called TTS, starts with written text and reads it aloud. Audio generation is broader: it can include speech, sound effects, music, or mixed audio. Voice cloning means generating speech that sounds like a specific person, usually from sample recordings of that person.

A model is a pattern-finding system trained on many audio examples. It learns relationships between text, speech sounds, timing, pitch and style. When given a prompt, it predicts a waveform, meaning the up-and-down signal that a speaker or headphone can play as sound.

This is often confused with speech-to-text, which does the reverse and turns spoken audio into written words. It is also confused with deepfakes. A cloned voice can be part of a deepfake, but not all generated speech is deceptive. For example, an accessibility tool that reads text aloud is generated speech without pretending to be a real recording.

everydayAnalogy.title: An announcer studio with reusable voice settings
everydayAnalogy.story: Imagine a radio station that has a script desk and a digital announcer console. A producer types a sentence, then chooses either a standard station voice or a saved voice profile that matches one presenter’s accent and pace. The console reads the new script aloud in seconds, even though that presenter never entered the studio. If the producer instead asks for crowd noise or a door closing sound, the system uses a different audio tool, because not all audio is speech.

mapping.aiElement: voice cloning setup based on sample recordings

mapping.analogyElement: separate tool for crowd noise or sound effects

everydayAnalogy.limitation: A real model does not keep neat, human-readable 'voice profiles' the way a studio might label presets. It works through learned statistical patterns in data. Also, the analogy makes the process seem fully controlled and reliable, but generated audio can mispronounce words, miss emotional cues, or produce misleadingly realistic imitations.

steps.label: Text-to-speech

steps.label: What it is not

visual.accessibilityDescription: The diagram compares three related tools. First, text-to-speech starts with written text and outputs spoken audio, usually in a built-in synthetic voice. Second, voice cloning starts with written text plus sample recordings of one person and outputs new speech that sounds similar to that person. Third, broader audio generation can start with prompts or reference audio and can output speech, music or sound effects. A note underneath explains that speech-to-text is the reverse process because it turns audio into text, and deepfake is a deceptive use of synthetic media rather than a synonym for all generated audio.

workedExample.scenario: A museum wants short audio guides in English, Arabic and Swahili for the same exhibit text.
workedExample.input: English script: 'This sculpture was created in 1962 and restored in 2018.' The team also has approved voice settings for a neutral guide voice.
process: Staff enter the sentence into a text-to-speech tool and choose the approved guide voice.
The tool generates spoken English audio in about 7 seconds.
Translators provide Arabic and Swahili text, and staff generate matching audio versions with suitable pronunciation settings.
The team listens to all three files, corrects one place name pronunciation, and exports final MP3 files for the guide app.
workedExample.result: The museum gets three short spoken clips from text inputs without booking a studio, but humans still check pronunciation, tone and factual accuracy.

unWorkplaceExample.scenario: A communications team in a UN country office prepares short public service audio notices in several languages for an approved outreach campaign.
unWorkplaceExample.relevance: Text-to-speech can speed up draft audio production, improve accessibility and help teams test wording before arranging final human narration or approved synthetic voices.
unWorkplaceExample.caution: Do not upload confidential, personal, protection-sensitive, security-sensitive or operational information to an unapproved public AI service, and do not clone a colleague’s or public figure’s voice without clear authorisation and safeguards.

whyItMatters: Non-specialists may hear a convincing voice and assume a real person recorded it. That is no longer a safe assumption. These tools can improve accessibility, multilingual communication and production speed, but they also make impersonation, fraud and false evidence easier. Knowing the difference between ordinary text-to-speech, voice cloning and broader audio generation helps you ask better questions: What was the source? Was consent given? Was it reviewed by a human? Is there provenance information, such as content credentials? Should this audio be trusted for a decision, or verified another way first?

commonMisconceptions.misconception: If audio sounds natural, it must be a real recording of a real person.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Generated speech can now sound very realistic, especially in short clips. Natural sound is not proof of authenticity. If the source matters, check who created it, whether the speaker consented, and whether there is independent verification or provenance information.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Text-to-speech, voice cloning and deepfake all mean the same thing.
commonMisconceptions.correction: They overlap but are not identical. Text-to-speech reads written text aloud, often in a generic synthetic voice. Voice cloning tries to match a specific person’s voice. Deepfake usually refers to deceptive synthetic media, which can include cloned audio but can also involve video or images.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: A cloned voice reproduces exactly what the person would have said or felt.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It only imitates patterns in recordings such as accent, pitch and rhythm. It does not provide reliable evidence of intent, emotion, truthfulness or approval by the person whose voice is being imitated.

simpleVsTechnical.simple: These tools create spoken sound from text or from examples of someone’s voice. Some just read text aloud in a computer voice. Others can make new audio that resembles a specific person or generate other kinds of sound.
simpleVsTechnical.technical: Modern systems for speech and audio generation learn statistical relationships between inputs such as text, phonemes, speaker examples and acoustic features, then produce audio signals. In text-to-speech, a system maps written words to pronunciation and prosody, meaning timing, stress and intonation, before generating a waveform. In voice cloning or speaker-conditioned synthesis, the model also uses features extracted from recordings of a target speaker so the output resembles that voice. Broader audio generation extends beyond speech to music, sound effects or mixed soundscapes. Different architectures can be used, including diffusion-based systems and other neural waveform or acoustic models. This should be distinguished from speech-to-text, which recognises words from incoming audio rather than generating new sound.

keyTakeaway: A believable voice clip may be synthetic, so treat generated audio as useful but not self-authenticating.

quickCheck.question: Which statement best distinguishes these related terms?
options: Speech-to-text creates spoken audio from written text, while text-to-speech turns speech into writing.
Voice cloning is one kind of audio and speech generation that aims to sound like a specific person, while text-to-speech may use a generic synthetic voice.
Deepfake means any computer-generated audio, including accessibility reading tools.
Audio generation only refers to music and sound effects, not speech.
quickCheck.explanation: Voice cloning is a narrower case within audio and speech generation. It targets the likeness of a particular voice. Text-to-speech may simply read text aloud without imitating a real person. Speech-to-text is the reverse direction, and deepfake refers to deceptive synthetic media rather than all generated audio.
